documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
55F transferring care. Here to get set up and keep her two regular meds going.

HTN: on amlodipine 5 mg for several years via her old office. No home cuff. No headaches, no palpitations, no ankle swelling.
Lipids: atorvastatin 20 mg, tolerates it fine, no muscle aches.
Takes acetaminophen 500 mg now and then for ordinary aches; no NSAIDs.

PSH: appendectomy at 16, gallbladder out at 42.
Allergies: PENICILLIN - anaphylaxis (as a young adult, needed epinephrine). IV CONTRAST - hives with a CT years ago.
FH: father had colon cancer at 67; his father also had colon cancer. Mother has osteoporosis.
SH: high school administrative assistant. Smoked ~15 pack-years, quit 2017. Wine 2-3 glasses a month. Married.

Screening: Pap/HPV done 2021 at old office, normal per pt. Mammogram 2021. Has been doing the stool kit (FIT) yearly; had a long talk with her old doctor about colonoscopy and prefers the kit for now. Discussed again given dad and grandfather; she knows colonoscopy is the stronger test, wants to keep FIT this year. Will send kit.

Exam: well, pleasant. BP as recorded. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed RLQ and laparoscopic scars. No peripheral edema.

A/P
1. HTN - at goal, continue amlodipine 5.
2. Hyperlipidemia - continue atorvastatin 20; fasting lipids, CMP, CBC today. A1c once.
3. Screening - HCV and HIV once today. FIT kit. Screening mammogram order. Old records requested.
4. Former smoker, 15 pk-yr - below the pack-year threshold for lung CT screening.
RTC 6 months.

LDL is right around 100 on the atorvastatin, which is fine for you. No changes. The stool kit should come in the mail within the week.

orders.reason: colorectal cancer screening; father and paternal grandfather with colorectal cancer

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
58F. Booked this in place of the physical she cancelled in June. Main agenda is colon cancer. She never sent back last year's FIT, and over the summer she has been reading about stool tests and wants to know how much a negative one is really worth for someone with her family.

No change in bowel habits, no blood, no black stools, no belly pain, appetite and weight steady by her account. Energy fine.

PMH: HTN, hyperlipidemia. PSH: appendectomy (16), cholecystectomy (42).
Meds: amlodipine 5 daily, atorvastatin 20 daily, acetaminophen 500 prn.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), iodinated contrast (hives).
FH: father colorectal cancer at 67, paternal grandfather colorectal cancer, mother osteoporosis.
SH: HS admin assistant; ex-smoker 15 pk-yr, quit 2017; wine 2-3 glasses/month.

Exam: BP charted. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no mass or organ enlargement.

Counseling, ~20 min: a stool test can miss cancers and many polyps; how reassuring a negative result is depends on how likely disease was to begin with. With a first-degree relative and a grandparent on the same side, her starting risk is higher than average, so a negative FIT tells her less than it would tell her neighbor. Colonoscopy both looks at the whole colon and removes polyps. She asked good questions and agrees to go ahead this time.

A/P
1. CRC screening, increased risk by family history - GI referral for colonoscopy; the overdue FIT order cancelled. She'll take the first opening.
2. HTN - at goal on amlodipine 5.
3. Hyperlipidemia - atorvastatin 20; lipids, CMP, CBC today since the physical slipped.
4. Mammogram due in the fall.
RTC after colonoscopy / physical in the winter.

reports.text: Specimen: ascending colon mass, cold forceps biopsies (6 fragments). Microscopic: fragments of colonic mucosa with invasive adenocarcinoma forming irregular glands with desmoplastic stroma; moderately differentiated. Background mucosa unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Ascending colon, biopsy: invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated.

documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - COLONOSCOPY REPORT (received 8/14/2025)
Date of procedure: 8/12/2025
Indication: colorectal cancer screening; father with colorectal cancer at 67, paternal grandfather with colorectal cancer. Prior screening by FIT.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), iodinated contrast (hives).
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Prep: split-dose, good (BBPS 8).
Findings: Scope advanced to the cecum, identified by the appendiceal stump and ileocecal valve; cecal photos taken. In the ascending colon, an ulcerated, friable, partially circumferential mass; the scope passed it. Multiple cold forceps biopsies obtained. Area tattooed distally with India ink. The remainder of the colon, transverse through rectum, without polyps or other lesions. Retroflexion in the rectum unremarkable.
Impression: ascending colon mass, suspicious for malignancy, biopsied and tattooed.
Plan: await pathology; CT chest/abdomen/pelvis and CEA; referral to colorectal surgery placed by our office. PCP notified.

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of colon
conditions.note: ascending colon adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, on colonoscopy biopsy

documents.title: Colonoscopy and pathology received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Colonoscopy report (8/12) and biopsy pathology received by fax from the GI group. Pathology positive for adenocarcinoma. Routed urgently to PCP.

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Patricia. GI had already told her about the mass after the procedure; today I went over the biopsy - it is a cancer (adenocarcinoma) of the right side of the colon. She was composed and had already written down questions. GI has ordered staging CT and CEA and referred her to colorectal surgery. Reminded her to tell radiology about her contrast hives so they can premedicate. She knows she can call or text me any time. Will follow along.

reports.text: Technique: helical CT of the chest with IV contrast, part of a chest/abdomen/pelvis staging exam. Patient premedicated with steroids and an antihistamine for prior contrast hives; no reaction. Findings: no pulmonary nodules or masses. No pleural effusion. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary adenopathy. Heart size normal. Visualized bones without lytic or blastic lesions.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of thoracic metastatic disease.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Technique: portal venous phase CT abdomen and pelvis after premedication. Findings: focal wall thickening/mass of the ascending colon at the site of the tattoo. No liver lesions. Surgically absent gallbladder and appendix. Spleen, pancreas, adrenals and kidneys unremarkable. No ascites. No retroperitoneal or pelvic adenopathy. No peritoneal nodularity. Bladder and uterus unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Known ascending colon primary. No evidence of distant metastatic disease.

documents.title: Staging CT and CEA received
documents.author: front desk

documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just wanted to let you know they did my surgery on Thursday the 28th - laparoscopic, right side of the colon taken out and reconnected. I came home Sunday. Sore but walking around the house. They said the oncologist will call once the pathology is final. Do I keep taking my blood pressure and cholesterol pills as usual?

documents.title: RE: Surgery done
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: So glad you are home. Yes, keep amlodipine and atorvastatin as usual; acetaminophen is fine for pain unless the surgeons told you otherwise. Let's do a quick video check next week - the front desk will reach out. Call sooner for fever, worsening belly pain, vomiting or redness at the incisions.

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt at her kitchen table. Two weeks after laparoscopic right hemicolectomy (8/28). Pain mild, acetaminophen once or twice a day. Eating small meals, bowels moving, no blood. No fever. Incisions look clean and closed on camera, no redness. Walking a bit more each day.
She was told the cancer had reached some lymph nodes and that she'll meet oncology later this month about chemo. We don't have the op note, discharge summary or final pathology yet.
Plan: continue home meds unchanged. Requesting hospital records. She'll message after the oncology visit. Mammogram can wait until treatment plans settle.

reports.text: Specimen: right colon and terminal ileum, laparoscopic right hemicolectomy. Tumor site: ascending colon. Histologic type: adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated. Tumor penetrates to the surface of the visceral peritoneum (pT4a). Proximal, distal and radial margins negative. Lymph nodes: 2 of 23 positive (pN1b). Mismatch repair immunohistochemistry: MLH1, PMS2, MSH2 and MSH6 retained (intact).
reports.conclusion: Adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon, pT4a pN1b, margins negative, MMR proficient. AJCC stage IIIB.

documents.author: colorectal surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY (received 10/7/2025 after second request)
Admitted 8/28/2025, discharged 8/31/2025. Service: colorectal surgery.
Diagnosis: adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon.
Procedure 8/28: laparoscopic right hemicolectomy with primary (stapled) ileocolic anastomosis.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis); iodinated contrast (hives).
Course: uncomplicated. Enhanced recovery pathway; clear liquids POD0, regular diet POD2, return of bowel function POD2. Pain controlled with scheduled acetaminophen. Ambulating independently.
Discharge meds: home amlodipine 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, acetaminophen 500 mg as needed.
Final pathology: pT4a N1b (2/23), margins negative, MMR intact - stage III. Referred to medical oncology for adjuvant therapy.
Follow-up: surgical clinic 2 weeks; medical oncology.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Check-in midway through adjuvant chemo. Oncology records still haven't come despite our request in October, so history is from Patricia and her pill bottles.

Stage IIIB ascending colon adenocarcinoma (pT4a N1b, 2/23 nodes, MMR intact) - lap right hemicolectomy 8/28. CAPOX started 10/16: oxaliplatin at the infusion center day 1, capecitabine 1,500 mg BID days 1-14, q21 days, plan for 8 cycles. Cycle 3 was 12/1; cycle 4 moved to 12/29 around the holidays. Bloodwork at the cancer center each cycle - she says they've been fine to proceed.

Feels wiped out for a few days after each infusion, then picks up. Mild nausea, ondansetron helps. Working shortened days. Weight down about 3 kg since summer, eating less. Mood okay; PHQ-9 4.

BP charted, at goal on amlodipine 5. Atorvastatin 20 continues.

Exam: tired-appearing but comfortable. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed laparoscopic incisions, nontender. No edema.

A/P
1. Colon cancer stage III on adjuvant CAPOX - oncology-run. Med list updated with capecitabine, oxaliplatin and ondansetron per patient. Re-requesting oncology notes.
2. HTN - controlled, continue.
3. Hyperlipidemia - continue atorvastatin; lipids from August fine.
4. Flu vaccine today (inactivated OK during chemo, she checked with oncology). Mammogram deferred until after treatment.
5. Weight - small meals, protein; oncology following.
RTC after chemo finishes, sooner prn.

documents.title: Diarrhea
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Since Wednesday I've had a lot of watery diarrhea, 6 or more times a day, even overnight. No fever and no blood. My next chemo was supposed to be Monday the 19th and the oncology nurse says they're holding it and getting me in with GI. I'm drinking as much as I can. Just keeping you posted.

documents.title: RE: Diarrhea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me. Glad oncology is on it and GI is involved. Keep sipping fluids with some salt and sugar in them (broth, oral rehydration drinks). Go to the ER or call oncology right away for fever, blood in the stool, dizziness when standing, or if you can't keep fluids down. Let me know what GI says.

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation (outside)
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - CONSULTATION LETTER (visit 1/29/2026; received 2/24/2026)
Referred by: medical oncology. cc: primary care.

Reason: watery diarrhea during adjuvant chemotherapy.

History: 58-year-old woman we know from her colonoscopy in August, now with stage III ascending colon adenocarcinoma after laparoscopic right hemicolectomy, on adjuvant CAPOX; also hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Her fourth cycle finished about three weeks ago and cycle 5 is on hold. Roughly two weeks ago she began passing six to eight large, watery brown stools a day, and they keep coming even when she eats nothing overnight. She took a 7-day course of clindamycin from her dentist, finishing 1/9 (penicillin anaphylaxis), and the diarrhea began a few days later. No travel, no sick contacts, nothing unusual eaten. Eating less, and down 3 kg since her last oncology visit. No fever, no blood in the stool, no abdominal pain.

Meds: amlodipine 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, acetaminophen 500 mg as needed; capecitabine and oxaliplatin per oncology (held); ondansetron as needed. Clindamycin completed.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), iodinated contrast (hives).
Family history: father and paternal grandfather with colorectal cancer; mother with osteoporosis.
Social: high school administrative assistant; former smoker (15 pack-years, quit 2017); wine 2-3 glasses a month.

Exam: vitals within normal limits. Alert, not toxic. Mucous membranes moist. Heart and lungs unremarkable. Abdomen: healed laparoscopic incisions, mild tenderness diffusely without rebound or guarding, normal bowel sounds, no mass. No edema.

Data (1/29): hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, WBC 5.0 K/uL, platelets 250 K/uL; sodium 140, potassium 3.5, creatinine 1.0. Stool C. difficile toxin negative. Fecal occult blood negative.

Impression: antibiotic-associated diarrhea due to clindamycin, C. difficile negative.

Recommendations: oral hydration with electrolyte drinks; we expect this to ease now that the antibiotic is finished. Timing of the next chemotherapy cycle is up to oncology once stools settle. Return to us as needed; she knows to call for fever, blood or worsening.

Thank you for involving us.

documents.title: Oncology treatment summary (outside)
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - TREATMENT SUMMARY AND SURVIVORSHIP PLAN
Diagnosis: adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon, pT4a pN1b (2/23), MMR proficient, stage IIIB. Laparoscopic right hemicolectomy 8/28/2025.
Adjuvant therapy: CAPOX x 8 cycles. Cycles 1-4 10/16/2025-12/29/2025. Cycle 5 delayed for clindamycin-associated diarrhea (seen by GI 1/29/2026, C. difficile negative), which resolved by early February. Cycles 5-8 given 2/9, 3/2, 3/23 and 4/13/2026; final capecitabine dose 4/26/2026. Treatment complete.
Surveillance: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast (premedicated) 6/23/2026 - no evidence of disease. CEA 1.6 ng/mL (pre-op 2.4).
Plan: CEA every 3-6 months and CT every 6-12 months; one-year surveillance colonoscopy with gastroenterology; return to primary care for routine care, blood pressure and cholesterol, and age-appropriate screening.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), iodinated contrast (hives) - premedicate for contrast studies.
